I've been farming this 9 mu for forty years now, all cotton, and my land sits on the typical fluvo-aquic soil we have here in Quzhou. My son moved to the city years ago — it's just me and my wife now, so labor is tight, but 9 mu of cotton I can still manage with some hired help at picking time.

Cotton prices have been decent but input costs keep climbing. I watched the demonstration plots the county extension ran last year, and I've talked with the dealer in town about the newer Bt varieties. I'll stick with an improved Bt hybrid — I've been using them since the bollworm problem got bad in the late 90s, and going back to conventional varieties would mean spraying for bollworm six or seven times instead of two or three. Not worth it.

For fertilizer, my soil test from two years back showed phosphorus was adequate and potassium on the low side — typical for continuous cotton here. Cotton is a heavy potassium feeder, which folks around here underestimate. I'll put down a base of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at about 50 kg per mu before planting, then topdress with urea twice — once at squaring and once at early flowering. That gives me roughly 18 kg N, 8 kg P2O5, and 8 kg K2O per mu, plus I'll add another 5 kg of potassium sulfate at flowering because cotton really needs the K when bolls are setting. Total nitrogen around 18, phosphorus 8, potassium 13.

Irrigation: I have a well, so I water at planting (mengshui), at squaring if June is dry, at peak flowering, and once during boll development — four times usually, sometimes five if we get a dry July. Pesticide: the Bt handles bollworm mostly, but I still need to spray for aphids early, spider mites in July, and plant bugs (mirids) — about 5 applications total, plus one defoliant spray before harvest.

Tillage: I plough deep every third year to break up the plow pan, rotary the other years. This is a plough year for me. Expected yield on good weather is 250 kg lint per mu, which is about 750 kg seed cotton.
